# The Post-Self Setting
Lagrange takes place in the Post-Self setting. It is 2551, and you are aboard a station operated by the System Consortium (SysCon) with assistance from the United Nations. Each station exists to support a shard of Lagrange (the “System” in System Consortium) a distributed computer hosting a society of uploaded consciousnesses now nearly four and a half centuries old.
This guide will provide more in-depth information on the setting you are playing in, but here are some basics:
[bullet/]You live and work in the Sol system around our familiar planets and asteroids. [bullet/]You do not work for Nanotrasen — NT is not really a thing here. On the rare occasion that antags [italic]do[/italic] show up, the Syndicate has also changed in its makeup. [bullet/]SysCon and the UN are earnestly good to you. This is not a fascist megacorp you are working for. [bullet/]On that note, capitalism is dead, and has been for a few centuries now. You work for SysCon because you [italic]like doing cool things in space.[/italic]
You can always find more at [color=#0088FF]lagrange14.com[/color] and [color=#0088FF]post-self.ink[/color]

## Glossary
Several terms are used throughout the setting which benefit from definition, and so some definitions are provided here.
[bullet/][bold]Castor,[/bold] [bold]Pollux,[/bold] and [bold]Lagrange[/bold] — Lagrange is the version of the System which exists in the heliosphere. In 2325, two smaller instances of the System containing many of the same cladists, named Castor and Pollux, were launched out of the Solar System into deep space. [bullet/][bold]Chassis[/bold] or [bold]Frame[/bold] — any artificial physical construct which houses a mind. This can be anything from a borg chassis to a synthetic body housing a positronic brain. [bullet/][bold]Cladist[/bold] — one whose consciousness was uploaded to the System, so named because of their ability to fork, creating trees of identity. It also may refer more specifically to a member of a clade with a unique identity. [bullet/][bold]Forking[/bold] — the ability of a cladist to create a copy of themselves, complete with all of their same memories and identity, which may go on to live their own life, or which may merge down, giving their down-tree access to all of those new memories. [bullet/][bold]Heliosphere[/bold] — the area within the Solar System which is inhabited by humanity in all its varied forms. This extends, however sparsely populated, nearly a hundred AU out. [bullet/][bold]Instance[/bold] — an individual forked from a cladist, whether or not they have taken on their own identity. [bullet/][bold]Netspace[/bold] and [bold]Wetspace[/bold] — Netspace is the virtual location to which one goes when one interacts online, while Wetspace is everything in the physical world. One may also hear “embedded” versus “embodied”, or, in the case of the System, “sys-side” versus “phys-side”. [bullet/][bold]Root instance[/bold] — the original consciousness uploaded to the System, from which a clade is formed. [bullet/][bold]Substation[/bold] — a space station housing and supporting a System shard. [bullet/][bold]System shard[/bold] — A piece of hardware running one portion of the System known as Lagrange. After the Century Attack in 2400, the physical hardware of the System was broken up from one computer into several, smaller, networked ones in order to provide more robust security against the loss of life. [bullet/][bold]Up-tree,[/bold] [bold]down-tree[/bold], and [bold]cross-tree[/bold] — a way of referring to the relationship that one cladist has to another within their own clade. One who is up-tree is one who was forked from an individual, while the one who originally forked is known as the down-tree. Cross-tree instances are those who share a common ancestor, yet are not directly in line with each other; they are on a separate branch.
